content:
- Finished the tests/ha/support boundary reduction task.
- Commit 65ff990 collapsed observer-local path and binary helper layers in tests/ha/support/observer/{sql,pgtm}.rs.
- Validation passed: make check; cargo nextest run --workspace --all-targets --profile default --no-tests fail host_postgres_dsn_quotes_tls_paths; cargo nextest run --workspace --all-targets --profile default --no-tests fail harness_settings_parse_into_resolved_paths.
- Ran bash .ralph/task_switch.sh successfully enough to update task files and send email, but it still printed rm: cannot remove .ralph/current_task.txt: No such file or directory.
- Verified that task-switch cleanup issue is already tracked in .ralph/tasks/bugs/bug-task-switch-missing-current-task-file.md, so no duplicate bug was created.
- If resuming later: ignore unrelated dirty .ralph/progress/task-summary files and the pre-existing .agents skill-file modification unless asked to handle them.

- Read prior progress and confirmed the last completed task was a different tests/ha/support boundary reduction.
- Loaded the improve-code-boundaries skill and started a fresh scan of tests/ha/support for one concrete wrapper/helper/type boundary to collapse.
- Next: inspect the support modules for pass-through helpers, duplicate shapes, or config/bootstrap DTO layers, then implement one narrow reduction and validate with make check plus focused cargo nextest.

- Scanned tests/ha/support for boundary smells and narrowed the most promising candidate to observer/pgtm: local routing/config helpers plus manual rendering around the observer command boundary.
- Current focus is verifying whether those helper structs/functions are just courier layers that can be collapsed into the real caller data.
- Next: read pgtm.rs and its world/steps call sites, remove one useless layer, then run make check and focused nextest.

- Read pgtm observer and related callers. The likely boundary smell is shifting from helper-string rendering toward early conversion of typed observer/routing failures into String buckets.
- Investigating whether member observations and write-convergence routing can keep HarnessError or a narrower typed error longer instead of flattening to String immediately.
- Next: inspect HarnessError and observation/convergence code for a contained typed-boundary collapse that still reduces code.

- Found and reported a bug per repo instructions: primary-count invariant currently swallows observer.state_via_member failures by turning them into Ok((member, false)).
- Added .ralph/tasks/bugs/bug-primary-count-invariant-swallows-observer-failures.md after confirming no duplicate bug file existed.
- Next: keep the actual improve-code-boundaries change narrow, likely in the same observer/invariant area, and avoid mixing in the bugfix unless the boundary collapse naturally includes it.

- Implemented the boundary reduction in tests/ha/support/invariants/primary_count.rs: member-success observations no longer courier (ClusterMember, bool) through every path.
- The runner now derives member identity from the fixed observation order, and I removed related dead code (empty impl block, now-unused test import).
- Next: run rustfmt if needed, then make check and focused cargo nextest on primary_count coverage before committing.

- Started validation with make check and a focused cargo nextest primary_count run.
- Validation briefly serialized on Cargo's build lock because both commands compiled the same workspace concurrently; nextest progressed first and make check is now actively checking.
- Next: collect both results, fix anything the linter/tests report, then commit and run .ralph/task_switch.sh.

- Validation passed: make check; cargo nextest run --workspace --all-targets --profile default --no-tests fail primary_count.
- Committed the boundary reduction and bug record as ae8bcd0 (Reduce primary count observation boundary). Post-commit docs hook completed successfully.
- Next: run bash .ralph/task_switch.sh, then note any task-switch errors (especially the previously-seen current_task cleanup issue) before exiting.
